question: Two circular ponds have circumferences in the ratio 3:5. If the smaller pond has an area of 150 m², what is the approximate area of the larger pond?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of areas = (Ratio of circumferences)²

Area ratio = 3² : 5² = 9 : 25

9 parts = 150 m²

25 parts = (150 ÷ 9) × 25 = 416.67 m²

Approximate area ≈ 417 m²

**∴ The correct answer is 417 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of circumferences of two circular ponds = 3 : 5

Area of the smaller pond = 150 m²

**Formula Used:**

Circumference of a circle = 2 × π × r

Area of a circle = π × r²

 
 
 
• 
 3x
 Smaller Pond
 Area = 150 m²
 
 
 
• 
 5x
 Larger Pond
 Area = ?

**Calculations:**

⇒ Ratio of circumferences = (2 × π × r₁) : (2 × π × r₂) = 3 : 5

⇒ Ratio of radii (r₁ : r₂) = 3 : 5

⇒ Ratio of their areas = (π × r₁²) : (π × r₂²) = r₁² : r₂²

⇒ Ratio of areas = 3² : 5² = 9 : 25

⇒ Let the area of the larger pond be A.

⇒ 9 / 25 = 150 / A

⇒ 9 × A = 150 × 25

⇒ 9 × A = 3750

⇒ A = 3750 ÷ 9

⇒ A = 416.66... m²

⇒ Approximating to the nearest whole number, A ≈ 417 m²

**∴ The correct answer is 417 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Scaling Principle for 2D Shapes

For any two similar 2D figures, the ratio of their areas is strictly equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding linear dimensions (e.g., radius, diameter, circumference, perimeter).

Ratio of Circumference vs Radius

Since the circumference of a circle is directly proportional to its radius (C = 2πr), the ratio of the circumferences of any two circles is exactly the same as the ratio of their radii or diameters.

Ratio of Volumes for 3D Shapes

If the objects were 3D spheres instead of 2D circles, the ratio of their volumes would be equal to the cube of the ratio of their linear dimensions (Volume Ratio = a³ : b³).
